safety_class_disclaimer.not_a_project_published_artefact_reason: This requirement belongs to the fictional reference project this corpus declares in its synthetic_reference profile, not to the foxBMS 2 product. foxBMS 2 published no requirement of any kind with an identifier, and nothing was ever allocated to an ASIL on its behalf. It states the reference project's mode-dependent reaction obligation, written by this corpus. Its own limitations field says it establishes nothing about the real foxBMS project.
safety_class_disclaimer.misreading_warning: A reader who sees an ASIL_D system requirement mandating mode-dependent reaction mapped to ISO 26262 Part 4 Clause 7 with status `mapped` will conclude the product selects its reaction by mode and never treats a degradation as a limit violation. The requirement is the reference project's, its record states the requirement was written because a corpus prompt insisted one contactor action is not unconditionally safe - so its existence is a response to an instruction, not an observation of the system, and the mode logic is not in the source.

statement: The item shall select its reaction according to the mode it is in and the nature of the condition, shall reach the safe state on a confirmed safe-operating-area violation in every mode, and shall enter its degraded mode rather than the safe state on a condition that its own monitoring has classified as degraded. The item shall publish the mode it is in and the reason for any departure from normal operation.
rationale: This requirement exists because the master prompt states that one contactor action is not unconditionally safe in every operating situation, and because the two other requirements in this set are silent about it. Opening the contactors in the traction mode removes propulsion; opening them in the charging mode removes a hazard; opening them in commissioning mode is not reachable at all. A requirement that says 'open the contactors on a violation' is therefore incomplete rather than merely conservative, because it does not say what the item does when the violation happens at speed.

acceptance_criteria.measure: Reaction type selected matching the mode's specified behaviour
Degraded conditions reacted to as safe-state conditions
Mode and departure reason published to the vehicle control unit

safety_allocation.mitigation: The per-mode fault reactions declared in the functional safety concept and realised by the software state machine

limitations: Synthetic. This requirement describes a hypothetical programme and establishes nothing about the real foxBMS project.

System-level only. It does not carry the hardware or software detail, which lives in FB2-HW-TSR-* and FB2-SW-SWR-*. Where this record and those records disagree, neither is silently preferred and the disagreement is raised as a finding.
